clusters.neutral_headline: Palantir patient data tech rejected by many NHS trusts in England

items.title: Palantir patient data tech rejected by many NHS trusts in England
items.standfirst: Exclusive: health bodies across country say controversial US firm’s data platform no better than systems already in useNHS organisations that care for millions of people in England are rejecting Palantir’s patient data technology, according to freedom of information responses that reveal health bosses believe they can find better or equal alternatives in many cases.Some health bodies said the £330m federated data platform (FDP) operated by the controversial US company had made it easier to manage waiting lists and has improved surgery scheduling. But, from Gateshead to Truro, others said they were declining to use it or had carried out trials and reverted to old systems. A Suffolk trust said other systems “supercede” the FDP’s functionality, while Greater Manchester’s care board called the Palantir system “duplicative” and “retrograde”. Continue reading...

clusters.title: The Letby case inquiry will lead to more blame and suspicion in the NHS – and patients will be less safe | Mark McDonald
clusters.neutral_headline: The Letby case inquiry will lead to more blame and suspicion in the NHS – and...

items.title: The Letby case inquiry will lead to more blame and suspicion in the NHS – and patients will be less safe | Mark McDonald
items.standfirst: I fear for what comes next because medics must be able to ask questions, raise concerns and admit mistakes. A defensive staff is dangerous for everyoneMark McDonald is a barrister representing Lucy LetbyI have been Lucy Letby’s barrister for the past two years. I have spent thousands of hours going through the evidence, speaking to experts and examining what happened to the babies who died or became seriously unwell on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester hospital. I have worked with nearly 30 experts, including internationally recognised specialists in neonatology, pathology, insulin, statistics and other fields. It may be to some an inconvenient truth, but I am convinced that Letby is innocent, and her convictions represent one of the most serious miscarriages of justice in modern British legal history. That means she was failed by the police, the NHS, the criminal justice system and, importantly, a plethora of experts who simply got it wrong.My work on the case has also raised wider concerns about the evidence and conclusions surrounding the deaths on the neonatal unit, and what the lessons being drawn from this case will mean for doctors and nurses in neonatal medicine.Mark McDonald is a criminal defence and human rights barrister specialising in miscarriages of justiceDo you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? clusters.title: Judith Lucy on her cancer diagnosis: ‘I’m a bit over getting so much material out of my life’
clusters.neutral_headline: Judith Lucy on her cancer diagnosis: ‘I’m a bit over getting so...

items.title: Judith Lucy on her cancer diagnosis: ‘I’m a bit over getting so much material out of my life’
items.standfirst: One of Australia’s hardest-working comedians is still laughing at the timing of a breast cancer diagnosis just as she set out to launch a book about wellness. Two days out from surgery, she talks burnout, Buddhism and saying goodbye to her boobsGet our weekend culture and lifestyle emailJudith Lucy cannot get a cold. A few hours before I’m due to meet her for a walk around the rose gardens and classic conservatory of the St Kilda Botanical Gardens, a stone’s throw from her home in Melbourne’s south-east, the beloved comedian is on a telehealth call from the front seat of her publicist’s car.Her doctor needs to go over the results from the previous day’s scans to confirm everything is looking good – good enough to perform the double mastectomy they have planned for Friday, three weeks after she was diagnosed with breast cancer. The cancer isn’t appearing anywhere else on the scans, she learns, but a compromised immune system going into surgery would throw the whole thing out of whack. So with the blustery wind and grey skies at our backs, we retreat into her home instead. The walk up and down the hallway, from the front door of her lovely weatherboard cottage to the neat living room at the back will have to make do for our very short walk. Continue reading...

items.standfirst: Millions affected by smoke from wildfires as schools close, respiratory illnesses soar and diplomatic tensions riseSingapore is threatening to prosecute companies responsible for some of the worst fires in years in neighbouring Indonesia, as the region grows increasingly frustrated with a persistent, acrid haze that could result in diplomatic relations fraying.Lawrence Wong, the Singaporean prime minister, said his government was distributing masks to vulnerable citizens and working with countries in the region to deal with the smoke. “At the same time, we are looking into which companies may be responsible for the fires,” he said in a Facebook post on Thursday, adding that he was exploring the idea of “joint action with other countries”.
